run.executedVia: Playwright runner, no browser: ServiceNow read over cnit and the Scripted REST API as sf.integration, Salesforce read over the sf CLI and anonymous Apex against the deployed classes. Every case reads both sides.

case.title: There is no named approver

steps.text: Read every approval record and resolve which belong to CAF tasks.
Check whether an approver identity is stored on the task itself.

records.label: Approval records belonging to CAF tasks
records.query: filtered client-side by document_id against caf_tsk.sys_id

observations: HANDOFF section 6 states sysapproval_approver holds no CAF records at all. TC-SN-059 found one, on CAFT0001002, created by the flow. This case re-reads that from the live instance.

The finding this case exists to make stands either way: whoever presses the button in Salesforce is the approver, and the audit trail records only sf.integration. For a compliance product that is the weakest point in the evidence chain — HANDOFF open item 2.
expected: No approver identity is stored on the task beyond sys_updated_by.
actual: 740 approval record(s) exist in total; 1 belong to CAF tasks.
10 task(s) carry an approved/rejected outcome; the only identity on them is sys_updated_by = admin, system, sf.integration.
case.verdictReason: Expected zero CAF approval records; found 1 — CAFT0001002 (created by system). The absence of a named approver still holds: none of these names a human approver of an attestation.
